full_judgment: 2. The petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.4 of 1994 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge Sadar. Comilla for declaration of title and recovery of Khas possession alleging, inter alia, that the opposite party who is a tenant under him has no title and possession. It was alleged that the opposite party has been serving in the police department and taking this advantage the opposite party in spite of ex parte decree obtained by him in Title Suit No. 4 of 1995 stood in the way of recovery of Khas possession for which he preferred Civil Revision No. 916 of 1997 before this Court against the order of the learned Assistant Judge, rejecting the prayer for striking out the name of the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 i.e., the Deputy Commissioner and Superintendent of Police, Comilla, It was further alleged that the civil revision was allowed and the name of the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 i.e. the Deputy Commissioner and Superintendent of Police. Comilla were struck off and, subsequently a date was fixed for ex parte disposal and accordingly, it was decreed ex parte on 10-6-97. The opposite party thereafter filed Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1998 under Order 9 rule 13 for setting aside the ex parte decree dated 10-6-97 and for restoration of the original suit to its file and number and the learned Assistant Judge allowed the Miscellaneous Case setting aside the ex parte decree and restoring the original suit to its file and number.
